second_order: keeping shared plans visible and editable
theme_note: These passages coordinate work by circulating agendas and templates, restoring missing plans, opening editing access, posting agreements, or handing agenda upkeep to someone else. What varies is whether access is by link, PM, repost, or moderator handoff.

second_order: adding and adjusting Doctor Who details
theme_note: These codes propose, complete, or fine-tune recognizable additions to the shared picture. The details vary from Ten and hearts to BAD WOLF, glasses, a sonic, and one-pixel symmetry; some are completed while others remain suggestions.

These passages direct pixels toward keeping existing work intact, cleaning stray or sexualized marks, answering attacks, and continuing the constant battle. They vary from priority-setting and repetitive maintenance to counter-pixels, time-zone relief, and explanations of why cleanup would not stay finished.

second_order: building borders and outlines to hold space
theme_note: These codes change the picture's enclosing structure—outline first, a surviving border tactic, and an expanded wall—to make the work easier to defend or to assert room. They vary between construction sequence, a partly deleted tactic, and territorial expansion.

second_order: deciding when an overlap is neighborly
theme_note: These passages work out whether shared pixels are attack, vandalism, harmless background use, or an agreed and even attractive overlap. Positions vary sharply: some cede content-less blue and stop undoing neighbors' work, while others feel betrayed, squeezed, extorted, or unsure the template will hold.

These codes seek representatives, make pleas and proposals, accept or contest deals, assign responsibility, and carry meaningful talk into Discord. What varies is authority (no fixed leader versus diplomats), tone (pleas, apology, anger), and whether a claimed agreement is accepted as settled.

second_order: bringing helpers together and returning help
theme_note: These passages recruit contributors, welcome them, rally allies, create communication access, authorize fans to speak, and send spare pixels to others. Help varies between the main Doctor Who group, nearby allies, tiny TARDIS projects, and people stepping into informal leadership; sometimes capacity is limited by work or burnout.

second_order: marking what survived and thanking the people who pixelled
theme_note: These post-event passages assess the final image, mourn damage, celebrate survival and immortality, thank participants and allies, share a timelapse, and ask about preserving the final canvas. The ending is mixed rather than unanimous: damaged in the final moments but still recognizable and worth congratulating.

second_order: recounting fatigue and time swallowed by pixels
theme_note: These codes look back on the cost of participation: tiring of the battle and losing a planned hour to templates, information, vandalism, and negotiation. One is a brief affective summary; the other gives the participant's own account of displaced leisure.

second_order: carrying pixel work onto a new canvas
theme_note: These passages invite the room to reuse its subreddit and contribute to a larger Doctor Who area after the original canvas closed. One supplies the venue; the other offers the community space for the continuation.
